Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
revision_notes: Original cited source (UNCDF South Sudan diagnostic report, Feb 2023) fetched and confirmed as authoritative and on-topic. Cross-checked against the World Bank Global Findex 2021 country brief and a GSMA (2023) analysis, both of which report that only 6% of South Sudanese adults (15+) held an account at a bank or mobile money provider in 2021 - the lowest rate of any economy surveyed - with mobile money account ownership below 1%. No more recent Findex round or national survey with a specific "active digital payment user" (90-day) metric was found for South Sudan. Given account ownership itself is only 6%, active digital payment usage is necessarily well under 20%, supporting the existing score of <20%. Score confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Digital payment uptake in South Sudan remains extremely low. Global Findex 2021 data show that only around 6% of adults (15+) hold an account at a bank or mobile money provider, with mobile money account penetration below 1% - the lowest financial inclusion rate recorded among Global Findex economies. No dedicated survey measuring active digital payment use over a 90-day period exists for South Sudan, but the low base of account ownership indicates that the active user share is well under 20% of the adult population.
